scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays product name, tagline, and call-to-action buttons correctly

steps.description: Open the MirDB landing page in a browser
steps.context: User discovers MirDB through search or referral

steps.description: Check that MirDB product name is prominently displayed with a compelling tagline
steps.context: Hero section should be above the fold

steps.description: Confirm primary CTA (Get Started/View on GitHub) and secondary CTA (Documentation) are visible
steps.context: CTAs should be clearly visible and clickable

test_cases.expected: Page contains 'MirDB' product name in prominent heading (h1)
Tagline mentions 'persistent', 'key-value', and 'Memcached' concepts
Primary CTA button exists with text like 'Get Started' or 'View on GitHub'
GitHub CTA links to valid GitHub repository URL

scenarios.name: Value Proposition Communication
scenarios.description: Verify the core value proposition (persistent key-value store with Memcached compatibility) is clearly communicated

steps.description: Scan the landing page for value proposition messaging
Confirm that persistence capability is highlighted as a key differentiator
Confirm Memcached protocol compatibility is mentioned
steps.context: Drop-in replacement value for existing Memcached users

test_cases.input: Search page content for persistence keywords
test_cases.expected: Page contains words like 'persistent', 'persistence', 'durable', or 'disk'

test_cases.input: Search page content for Memcached keywords
test_cases.expected: Page contains 'Memcached', 'protocol', and 'compatible' or 'compatibility'
Page explains that unlike Memcached, MirDB persists data to disk

scenarios.name: Features Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify key features are showcased in a card-based layout with accurate descriptions

steps.description: Scroll to or locate the features section of the page
Check that features are displayed in card or similar visual format
steps.context: Should include: Memcached protocol, persistence, LSM tree, Tokio async

steps.description: Confirm each feature has a clear, accurate description
steps.context: Technical accuracy is important for developer audience

test_cases.expected: Page contains a features section with identifiable feature cards/items
Feature card mentions Memcached protocol compatibility/support
Feature card mentions data persistence with SSTables
Feature card mentions LSM Tree architecture
Feature mentions async networking or Tokio
At least 3 feature cards are displayed

scenarios.name: Quick Start Guide
scenarios.description: Verify quick-start guide provides clear installation and usage instructions

steps.description: Find the quick-start or getting started section
Check for cargo build or installation commands
steps.context: Rust project uses cargo for building

steps.description: Check for basic usage examples showing how to connect

test_cases.expected: Page contains quick-start, getting-started, or installation section
Quick-start section contains 'cargo build' or 'cargo run' command

test_cases.input: Verify code blocks are syntax highlighted
test_cases.expected: Code examples use <pre><code> or similar markup with syntax highlighting
Instructions reference port 12333 (default MirDB port)

scenarios.name: Code Examples Display
scenarios.description: Verify code examples demonstrate basic SET/GET operations

steps.description: Find code examples showing MirDB usage
Check for SET command example
Check for GET command example

test_cases.expected: Page contains code examples section with syntax-highlighted code blocks
Code examples include SET command usage
Code examples include GET command usage
Example shows connecting using standard memcached client

scenarios.name: GitHub Repository Link
scenarios.description: Verify GitHub repository link is prominently displayed and functional

steps.description: Find GitHub repository link on the page
Confirm link is easy to find (header, hero, or footer)
steps.context: Should be discoverable without scrolling extensively

steps.description: Confirm link points to valid GitHub URL

test_cases.expected: Page contains at least one link to github.com

test_cases.input: Verify GitHub link in hero section
test_cases.expected: Hero section CTA includes GitHub link
Footer contains GitHub repository link

scenarios.description: Verify supported Memcached commands are listed

scenarios.name: Responsive Design - Mobile
scenarios.description: Verify page is responsive and mobile-friendly

steps.description: View page at mobile viewport width (375px)
Confirm content fits within viewport without horizontal scrolling
Confirm text is readable without zooming

test_cases.expected: All content visible without horizontal scrolling
Page includes proper viewport meta tag for mobile
Layout adapts appropriately for tablet size
Buttons and links have adequate touch target size (44x44px minimum)

scenarios.name: Cross-Browser Compatibility
scenarios.description: Verify page renders correctly on modern browsers

steps.description: Load page in Chrome and verify rendering
Load page in Firefox and verify rendering
Load page in Safari and verify rendering
Load page in Edge and verify rendering

test_cases.expected: HTML passes W3C validation without critical errors

test_cases.input: Verify no vendor-specific CSS without fallbacks
test_cases.expected: CSS uses standard properties or includes appropriate fallbacks
All sections render correctly, no visual bugs
All sections render correctly, no visual bugs

steps.description: Load page and measure time to interactive
Verify images and assets are optimized
Execute Lighthouse performance audit

test_cases.expected: Page loads within 2 seconds on standard broadband
CSS is minified or reasonably sized (< 50KB)
JavaScript is minimal or absent for core content
Lighthouse performance score > 80

scenarios.name: Accessibility Compliance
scenarios.description: Verify page meets accessibility requirements (WCAG 2.1 AA)

steps.description: Verify proper h1-h6 heading structure
Verify text has sufficient contrast ratio
steps.context: WCAG 2.1 AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text

steps.description: Verify all interactive elements are keyboard accessible
Verify all images have alt text

test_cases.expected: Page has exactly one h1 element
Headings follow proper sequence (no skipping levels)
All img elements have alt attributes
All interactive elements reachable via Tab key
Links have descriptive text, no 'click here' generic text
Text meets WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1 for normal, 3:1 for large)
